summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2M.4 repointed the active HMIC CertificationBinding on hac-dell from the old v1.6/36 certification (2e5f861249d8e70bff53ba2f371d84e37e14eff0bbfcd939902fa7b47d236bd7) to the new, already-created v1.7/38 certification (de110d41e6e094b55b3455e31f7dd5e17db8bbaa1e9a045d8920adc431de1609) via the governed scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py activate ceremony, run as the Protected Admin (root) OS principal against the deployed source at commit 4efcb255ca5340224f0278f724b939d794a553ca (unchanged from 2M.2/2M.3, freshly re-verified clean at phase entry). This is the first phase in this lineage to exercise successor-binding-replacement (an existing active binding pointing OLD being explicitly repointed to NEW) -- distinct from 149O.20L.7O.2K.5's first-ever activation with no prior binding. Independently proved permitted and safe from current source (_write_active_binding's own docstring: 'Plain locked replacement, never compare-and-swap ... whichever write completes second is the one that determines the final active pointer') and exercised via 9 new disposable tmp_path-isolated tests (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2m_4_hac_dell_hmic_v1_7_38_certification_activation_successor_binding_only.py) covering binding-switches-exactly-once, both-records-unchanged, validator-transitions-mismatch-to-valid, idempotent-reactivation-of-already-new-binding, unknown-certification-id-rejected, revoked-new-certification-can-be-bound-but-validator-reports-revoked, malformed-certifications-file-fails-closed, conflicting-repository-state-yields-wrong-repository, and no-other-protected-state-mutation -- all 9 passed in isolation before the real-host ceremony ran. A fresh Protected Admin election and human confirmation were obtained directly via an explicit interactive question presenting the exact target tuple (certification_id=de110d41..., repository_instance_id=0107866f-af7c-40b4-8317-74e71acb05ca, canonical_deployment_root=/opt/pcae/runtime/src) before any write occurred, distinct from and not reusing 2M.2/2M.3/2K.5's prior elections. Immediately before write: hostname/machine-id, deployed revision, and tree cleanliness were re-checked unchanged; live HMIC v1.7/38 identity was re-derived matching the precomputed target exactly; pre-activation inventory confirmed exactly 2 certifications (no third/malformed) and 1 binding pointing OLD; pre-activation validator confirmed IMPLEMENTATION_MISMATCH/readiness False. Executed exactly the existing production activate ceremony (sudo root, deployed venv, --repository-root /opt/pcae/runtime/src --certification-id de110d41... --assume-yes under the fresh interactive authorization) -- no internal writer called directly, no manual JSON edit. Post-activation, independently re-derived (never inferred from the ceremony's own exit code): both CertificationRecords read back through the production parser are field-for-field identical to their pre-activation state (certifications.json file mtime itself unchanged, confirming activation never touches this file); certification-bindings.json now contains exactly 1 binding, active_certification_id=de110d41e6e094b55b3455e31f7dd5e17db8bbaa1e9a045d8920adc431de1609 (the NEW certification) -- the OLD certification_id is no longer the active target, but the OLD CertificationRecord itself remains present and unmodified; the production validator, re-run fresh, transitioned IMPLEMENTATION_MISMATCH -> VALID; certification_status_satisfies_readiness transitioned False -> True. A fresh assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness call (root context, informational only -- not the canonical pcae+venv context HMIC-001's Class-B convention specifies for an authoritative verdict) confirmed only the mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified term flipped to satisfied; the remaining seven readiness terms (structurally independent of the certification-binding file -- they never read certifications.json/certification-bindings.json) are unaffected, so HATP overall readiness correctly remains False (NOT READY/NOT ACTIVE); activate_hatp_mandatory was never invoked. /etc/pcae/hatp/ listing after activation contains only the trust-store directory's three protected files -- no HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding file or directory anywhere; neither Trust-Enrollment admin script was invoked; no FIDO2/PIV hardware was touched at any point. Regression: a filtered -k "hmic or certification or hatp_mandatory" run showed 244 failed with this phase's new test file present vs 243 failed with it deselected -- the single-node delta (this phase's own test_unknown_certification_id_rejected, which independently passes in isolation) was confirmed to be the identical pre-existing suite-order-dependent flake class already present in the untouched, pre-existing 149O.20L.7O.2K.3 test node (test_activate_on_unknown_id_fails_closed, also fails combined, also passes isolated) -- not a regression introduced by this phase. Fast Green (python -m pytest -m fast_green, full non-tail-truncated): raw failure/pass counts (8592 passed, 4 skipped, 9 errors) match, in kind and magnitude, 149O.20L.7O.2M.3's own recorded post-change baseline (8583 passed), the same pre-existing stale-frozen-file-count assertions and HBDC-25-file/Class-B-conformance environment-dependent failures already disclosed as pre-existing debt. Zero attributable source/logic regressions from this phase's own change. Recommends the next real-effect Trust-Enrollment node be independently selected after re-deriving post-activation state, not automatically FIDO2 enrollment.
